Order matters: longer prefixes first.\nconst SUBJECT_TRIM_PREFIXES = [\n  \"the country called \",\n  \"the country \",\n  \"country \",\n  \"the city of \",\n  \"the city \",\n  \"city of \",\n  \"country called \",\n  \"republic of \",\n  \"kingdom of \",\n  \"is \",\n  \"in \",\n  \"of the \",\n  \"of \",\n  \"страна \",\n  \"страны \",\n  \"стране \",\n  \"страну \",\n];\n\nfunction trimSubjectTerm(raw) {\n  let value = String(raw || \"\")\n    .replace(/[«»\"'`“”„‟‹›]+/g, \"\")\n    .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n    .trim();\n  let changed = true;\n  while (changed) {\n    changed = false;\n    const lower = value.toLowerCase();\n    for (const prefix of SUBJECT_TRIM_PREFIXES) {\n      if (lower.startsWith(prefix)) {\n        value = value.slice(prefix.length).trim();\n        changed = true;\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return value;\n}\n\nfunction parseFactQuestion(prompt, normalized) {\n  const text = String(prompt || \"\");\n  if (!text.trim()) return null;\n  for (const pattern of FACT_QUESTION_PATTERNS) {\n    for (const regex of pattern.extract) {\n      const match = regex.exec(text);\n      if (!match) continue;\n      const subjectTerm = trimSubjectTerm(match[1]);\n      if (!subjectTerm) continue;\n      // Reject single-letter or pure-punctuation captures so we don't fire\n      // on noise like \"x.\" or \"?\".\n      if (subjectTerm.length < 2 && !/[Ѐ-鿿]/.test(subjectTerm)) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      return {\n        relation: pattern.relation,\n        subjectTerm,\n        language: detectLanguage(prompt),\n        forceFresh: shouldForceFresh(normalized, prompt),\n      };\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n// In-memory cache. Keyed by `relation:subject_normalized:language`. The TTL\n// matches the user-requested 1 week. Pre-warmed from FACTS at init() so the\n// offline test matrix sees the same starting cache the Rust solver does.\nconst FACT_QUERY_CACHE = new Map();\nconst FACT_QUERY_TTL_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n\nfunction factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language) {\n  return [\n    String(relation || \"\").toLowerCase(),\n    String(subjectTerm || \"\")\n      .toLowerCase()\n      .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n      .trim(),\n    String(language || \"en\").toLowerCase(),\n  ].join(\":\");\n}\n\nfunction factCacheGet(relation, subjectTerm, language) {\n  const key = factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language);\n  const entry = FACT_QUERY_CACHE.get(key);\n  if (!entry) return null;\n  if (\n    entry.expiresAt &&\n    typeof entry.expiresAt === \"number\" &&\n    entry.expiresAt < Date.now()\n  ) {\n    FACT_QUERY_CACHE.delete(key);\n    return null;\n  }\n  return entry;\n}\n\nfunction factCachePut(relation, subjectTerm, language, value) {\n  const key = factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language);\n  const ttl = typeof value.ttlMs === \"number\" ? value.ttlMs : FACT_QUERY_TTL_MS;\n  const entry = Object.assign({}, value, {\n    expiresAt: Date.now() + ttl,\n  });\n  FACT_QUERY_CACHE.set(key, entry);\n  return entry;\n}\n\n// Pre-warm the runtime cache from the seed `facts.lino`. We return a shared promise so concurrent\n// callers cooperate on the same probe batch.\nfunction ensureWebSearchProviderProbes() {\n  if (WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE) return WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE;\n  if (typeof fetch !== \"function\") {\n    WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE = Promise.resolve([]);\n    return WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE;\n  }\n  WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE = (async () => {\n    const tasks = WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDERS.map((provider) => async () => {\n      if (!provider.probeUrl) return null;\n      const startedAt = Date.now();\n      try {\n        const response = await fetch(provider.probeUrl, { mode: \"cors\" });\n        const status = response ? Tasks are async functions returning a value; results are\n  // returned in the original order.\n  const cap = Math.max(1, Math.min(limit, tasks.length));\n  const results = new Array(tasks.length);\n  let cursor = 0;\n  async function worker() {\n    while (true) {\n      const index = cursor;\n      cursor += 1;\n      if (index >= tasks.length) return;\n      results[index] = await tasks[index]();\n    }\n  }\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: cap }, () => worker()));\n  return results;\n}\n\nfunction reciprocalRankFusion(perProviderResults, k) {\n  // R194: the Rust/WASM core owns the fusion logic so the offline trace and\n  // the browser worker agree to the last byte. We try WASM first and only\n  // fall back to the JS implementation when the worker booted in\n  // `js fallback` mode (e.g. WASM disabled in the browser).\n  const wasmFused = wasmReciprocalRankFusion(perProviderResults);\n  if (wasmFused !== null) {\n    return wasmFused;\n  }\n  // Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher 2009: score(d) = Σ 1 / (k + rank_i(d)).\n  const fused = new Map();\n  for (const provider of perProviderResults) {\n    const list = Array.isArray(provider.results) ? provider.results : [];\n    list.forEach((item, index) => {\n      if (!item || !item.url) return;\n      const rank = index + 1;\n      const score = 1 / (k + rank);\n      const existing = fused.get(item.url);\n      if (existing) {\n        existing.score += score;\n        existing.providers.push({ id: provider.id, rank });\n        if (!existing.title && item.title) existing.title = item.title;\n        if (!existing.excerpt && item.excerpt) existing.excerpt = item.excerpt;\n      } else {\n        fused.set(item.url, {\n          url: item.url,\n          title: item.title || item.url,\n          excerpt: item.excerpt || \"\",\n          score,\n          providers: [{ id: provider.id, rank }],\n        });\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  return Array.from(fused.values()).sort((a, b) => {\n    if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;\n    return b.providers.length - a.providers.length;\n  });\n}\n\n// Issue #153/#180: identify \"the same entity\" returned by different providers\n// so the fused list shows one bullet with the other URLs collapsed under\n// \"Other sources:\". A single result can carry several canonical identifiers\n// (Wikidata Q-id, Wikipedia page key, Wiktionary headword) — dedupe walks all\n// of them and merges into the first existing group it finds. Returning a\n// list makes the Wikipedia↔Wikidata merge robust against percent-encoding\n// differences in the two providers' URLs.\nfunction canonicalEntityKeys(meta) {\n  if (!meta) return [];\n  const keys = [];\n  if (meta.qid && /^Q\\d+$/.test(meta.qid)) keys.push(`Q:${meta.qid}`);\n  if (meta.wikipediaKey) {\n    const lang = meta.wikipediaLanguage || \"en\";\n    keys.push(`WP:${lang}:${meta.wikipediaKey}`);\n  }\n  if (meta.wiktionaryKey) {\n    const lang = meta.wiktionaryLanguage || \"en\";\n    keys.push(`WT:${lang}:${meta.wiktionaryKey}`);\n  }\n  return keys;\n}\n\n// Backwards-compatible shim: prefer the primary key but keep the historical\n// single-key signature for callers that still rely on it.\nfunction canonicalEntityKey(meta) {\n  const keys = canonicalEntityKeys(meta);\n  return keys.length > 0 ? keys[0] : null;\n}\n\nfunction buildItemMetadataIndex(perProvider) {\n  // The richer the meta the better — an entry that carries a Wikidata `qid`\n  // is preferred over a Wikipedia-only entry for the same URL, because the\n  // Q-id is what cross-provider dedupe groups by. Without this preference,\n  // the Wikipedia URL would be indexed by the Wikipedia provider's meta\n  // (`WP:en:Apple`) and a separate Wikidata entry for the same fact (`Q:Q89`)\n  // would never collapse into one bullet.\n  const byUrl = new Map();\n  const rank = (item) => (item && item.qid ? 2 : 1);\n  function record(url, item) {\n    if (!url || !item) return;\n    const existing = byUrl.get(url);\n    if (!existing || rank(item) > rank(existing)) {\n      byUrl.set(url, item);\n    }\n  }\n  for (const provider of perProvider) {\n    if (!provider || !Array.isArray(provider.results)) continue;\n    for (const item of provider.results) {\n      if (!item || !item.url) continue;\n      record(item.url, item);\n      // Wikidata results carry the Wikipedia URL of the same entity inline;\n      // index that too so the Wikipedia provider's entry is recognised as\n      // a duplicate of the Wikidata one.\n      if (item.wikipediaUrl) record(item.wikipediaUrl, item);\n    }\n  }\n  return byUrl;\n}\n\nfunction dedupeFusedEntries(fused, metaByUrl, evidence) {\n  const groupsByKey = new Map();\n  const allGroups = [];\n  const standalone = [];\n\n  function alreadyHasProvider(target, candidate) {\n    return target.providers.some(\n      (existing) => existing.id === candidate.id && existing.rank === candidate.rank,\n    );\n  }\n\n  fused.forEach((entry, index) => {\n    const meta = metaByUrl.get(entry.url) || null;\n    const keys = canonicalEntityKeys(meta);\n    const enriched = Object.assign({}, entry, {\n      qid: (meta && meta.qid) || \"\",\n      wikipediaKey: (meta && meta.wikipediaKey) || \"\",\n      wikipediaLanguage: (meta && meta.wikipediaLanguage) || \"\",\n      wiktionaryKey: (meta && meta.wiktionaryKey) || \"\",\n      wiktionaryLanguage: (meta && meta.wiktionaryLanguage) || \"\",\n      sourceKind: (meta && meta.sourceKind) || \"\",\n      virtualId:\n        (meta && meta.virtualId) ||\n        (meta && meta.qid) ||\n        (meta && meta.wikipediaKey ? `WP:${meta.wikipediaKey}` : \"\"),\n      alternateUrls: [],\n      keys: keys.slice(),\n      originalRank: index,\n    });\n\n    if (keys.length === 0) {\n      standalone.push(enriched);\n      return;\n    }\n    let head = null;\n    for (const key of keys) {\n      if (groupsByKey.has(key)) {\n        head = groupsByKey.get(key);\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n    if (!head) {\n      allGroups.push(enriched);\n      for (const key of keys) {\n        if (!groupsByKey.has(key)) groupsByKey.set(key, enriched);\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n    // Found an existing group — absorb this entry into it.\n    head.score += enriched.score;\n    head.alternateUrls.push({\n      url: enriched.url,\n      title: enriched.title,\n      providers: enriched.providers,\n      sourceKind: enriched.sourceKind,\n    });\n    for (const p of enriched.providers) {\n      if (!alreadyHasProvider(head, p)) head.providers.push(p);\n    }\n    // Register the absorbed entry's keys against the head group too so a third\n    // provider matching either canonical id still merges in.\n    for (const key of keys) {\n      if (!groupsByKey.has(key)) groupsByKey.set(key, head);\n    }\n    // Prefer the richest virtualId once we know more identifiers.\n    if (!head.virtualId && enriched.virtualId) head.virtualId = enriched.virtualId;\n    if (!head.qid && enriched.qid) head.qid = enriched.qid;\n    if (!head.wikipediaKey && enriched.wikipediaKey) {\n      head.wikipediaKey = enriched.wikipediaKey;\n      head.wikipediaLanguage = enriched.wikipediaLanguage;\n    }\n    if (!head.wiktionaryKey && enriched.wiktionaryKey) {\n      head.wiktionaryKey = enriched.wiktionaryKey;\n      head.wiktionaryLanguage = enriched.wiktionaryLanguage;\n    }\n    if (Array.isArray(evidence)) {\n      evidence.push(`web_search:dedupe:${keys[0]}:absorbed:${enriched.url}`);\n    }\n  });\n  const merged = [...allGroups, ...standalone];\n  merged.sort((a, b) => {\n    if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;\n    if (b.providers.length !== a.providers.length) {\n      return b.providers.length - a.providers.length;\n    }\n    // Issue #180: stable order by provider priority so DDG-led entries beat\n    // Wikidata-only entries on perfect ties.\n    const ap = providerPriorityScore(a.providers);\n    const bp = providerPriorityScore(b.providers);\n    if (ap !== bp) return ap - bp;\n    return a.originalRank - b.originalRank;\n  });\n  return merged;\n}\n\nfunction providerPriorityScore(providers) {\n  if (!Array.isArray(providers) || providers.length === 0) return 999;\n  let best = 999;\n  for (const p of providers) {\n    const score = WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER_PRIORITY[p && p.id] || 999;\n    if (score < best) best = score;\n  }\n  return best;\n}\n\n// Issue #153: {\n  const haystack = String(normalized || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  const raw = String(prompt || \"\");\n  const rawLower = String(prompt || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  for (const { verb, op } of fuzzyPrefixMatch(prompt, entry.verb);\n      return match ? Object.assign({ entry }, match) : null;\n    })\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .sort((left, right) =>\n      left.typoCount - right.typoCount || right.end - left.end,\n    );\n  const best = matches[0];\n  if (!best) return null;\n  const peers = matches.filter(\n    (match) => match.typoCount === best.typoCount && match.end === best.end,\n  );\n  if (peers.length > 1) {\n    return {\n      ambiguous: true,\n      suggestions: peers.map((match) => match.entry.verb),\n      interpretations: [],\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    op: best.entry.op,\n    verb: best.entry.verb,\n    objectText: String(prompt || \"\").slice(best.end),\n    interpretations: [best.interpretation],\n  };\n}\n\nfunction detectFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized) {\n  return exactFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized) || fuzzyFormalizationMatch(prompt);\n}\n\nfunction objectForFormalization(prompt, normalized, match) {\n  // For search-style ops we extract the explicit query the same way the web\n  // search handler does. #221 demands\nthat the **same machinery works for any common noun**, in any direction\nbetween the supported languages, in **both** the Rust CLI and the\nbrowser demo, *without LLMs*.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date (UTC) | Event |\n| --- | --- |\n| 2026-05-19 | PR #208 lands the Wiktionary + Wikidata translation pipeline. |\n| 2026-05-21 | PR #211 fixes translation handler precedence and adds the compositional ru→en fallback. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #216 — `translate apple to russian` returns `[ru]`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #217 — `переведи «яблоко» на английский` returns `\"[en] яблоко\"`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Umbrella issue #218 opened; PR #219 fixes the apple noun for all four supported languages and lands a multilingual coverage CI guard. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #221 — the same fix does not cover `помидор` / `огурец` and the request escalates to **all** common nouns plus *texts of any size*. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Branch `issue-221-77aad836fb28` cut; PR #222 prepared. |\n| 2026-05-21 | CLI reproduction confirms the placeholder lives in two places: the offline cache only has `яблоко`, and the browser registry only has `apple`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Cache seed list expanded from 1 noun to 71×4 + 71 pairs; `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` ships the result as `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` so the browser worker can resolve common nouns without CORS-blocked API calls. |\n| 2026-05-21 | `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` verbose tracing added to the Rust pipeline (issue #218 \"Future work\" item). |\n\n## Requirements (from issue #221)\n\n1. Stop faking translation — no `[en] X` / `[ru] X` placeholders for\n   any common noun in any supported direction.\n2. Use Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wiktionary as the only sources of\n   meaning — the symbolic AI pipeline must remain LLM-free.\n3. Follow the *source → meta → target* flow already proven in #218:\n   `formalize(source) → meaning_id (Q/L/sense) → deformalize(target)`.\n4. Solve everything in a single pull request that **actually works**,\n   not just for one phrase but for arbitrary text size.\n5. Compile all logs and data into `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/`,\n   reconstruct the timeline, list every requirement, find every root\n   cause, and propose solutions. Search externally for additional data.\n6. Add debug output and a verbose mode if a root cause cannot yet be\n   pinned down.\n7. Report upstream defects against any external repo (Wiktionary,\n   Wikidata, etc.) that surface during investigation.\n\n## Artifacts\n\nLocal artifacts captured during investigation live under `raw-data/`:\n\n- `repro-pomidor-before-fix.log`, `repro-ogurec-before-fix.log` — CLI\n  reproductions before any change. Offline cache miss → `[en] помидор`.\n- `repro-pomidor-live-api.log`, `repro-ogurec-live-api.log` — same\n  prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`. Pipeline resolves\n  помидор→tomato and огурец→cucumber correctly, proving the algorithm\n  works and the gap is data-seeding-only.\n- `test-before-fix.log` — output of the new `issue_221_*` tests before\n  any seeding change, showing two failures (картофель/potato) and one\n  pass (помидор/огурец, because earlier live-API runs had already\n  warmed those entries).\n\n`online-research.md` collects the external references used while\ndiagnosing the bug (Wiktionary CORS policy, MediaWiki `origin=*`\nconvention, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint behaviour for polysemous lexemes).\n\n## Root Causes\n\n1. **Offline cache only contained one noun (`яблоко` / `apple`).**\n   `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` was the single source of\n   ground-truth data fed to the offline pipeline, and PR #219 added\n   only the apple pair. Every other common noun returned an `HttpError::\n   Transport(... cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active)`,\n   which the handler renders as `[en] помидор`. Verified by re-running\n   the same prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` — the pipeline succeeds\n   immediately (logs in `raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`).\n2. **Browser worker only consulted a hand-curated registry.**\n   `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` was\n   built up phrase-by-phrase. Words missing from the registry fell\n   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). The Rust\n   pipeline never runs in the browser — the worker is the only code\n   that handles in-browser translation, and the existing infrastructure\n   for live Wiktionary calls (e.g. `fetchWiktionaryEntry`) is only used\n   for the *external lookup* fallback, not for translation.\n3. **No automated bridge between the Rust ground truth and the JS\n   worker.** Even when PR #219 added the apple noun in both places, the\n   data lived in two unrelated source files; nothing kept them in sync.\n4. **No verbose mode in the pipeline.** When tests failed, the only\n   signal was a single line of output. Issue #218 explicitly listed\n   `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` as future work.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/translation/pipeline.rs`: add `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`\n  verbose tracing through every stage (`stage1` source-edition,\n  reverse, variants, Wikidata upgrade, compositional fallback). When\n  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n  distinguished in a single run.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs`: grow the seed list from one\n  noun + greetings to **71 English nouns × 4 targets and 71 Russian\n  nouns × 1 target** — every word listed in the demo / regression set\n  the issue exemplifies. `pairs` is now built procedurally so future\n  expansions stay readable.\n\n### Pre-compiled offline dictionary\n\n- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (new): runs the cached\n  pipeline against the full seed list and emits\n  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json`. Schema:\n\n  ```json\n  {\n    \"version\": 1,\n    \"entries\": …,\n    \"alias_count\": …,\n    \"by_lemma\": {\n      \"en\": { \"tomato\": { \"ru\": \"помидор\", \"hi\": \"टमाटर\", \"zh\": \"番茄\" } },\n      \"ru\": { \"помидор\": { \"en\": \"tomato\" } }\n    },\n    \"aliases\": {\n      \"ru\": { \"помидора\": \"помидор\", \"помидору\": \"помидор\", … },\n      \"en\": { \"tomatoes\": \"tomato\", … }\n    }\n  }\n  ```\n\n  Inflection forms are generated deterministically — Russian\n  declension suffixes by ending class and English plural rules — so\n  `Переведи \"помидоры\" на английский.` resolves to `tomato` without\n  another network call.\n\n### Browser worker\n\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: `loadTranslationDictionary()` fetches\n  the JSON above during `init()` (alongside the existing seed loader),\n  and `translateSurface` consults `lookupDictionary(...)` before\n  falling back to the hand-curated registry / placeholder. The fetch\n  is same-origin (no CORS), and the JSON ships as a static asset.\n- The browser worker can therefore resolve every common noun in the\n  seed list **without** crossing the network, while keeping the\n  existing registry as a back-up for greeting phrases.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three new tests\n  — `issue_221_common_russian_nouns_translate_to_english`,\n  `issue_221_common_english_nouns_translate_to_russian`, and\n  `issue_221_unquoted_common_noun_works_in_all_languages` — fail\n  loudly when any of помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or\n  their English counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — same prompts as the Rust tests, plus the round-trip\n  `ru→en→ru` to prove the dictionary keeps semantics symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.log` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; three new `issue_221_*` tests pass.\n- `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 cargo run --release --example refresh_translation_cache`\n  — no gaps in the new seed list (rerun once a quarter to refresh).\n- `cargo run --release --example build_translation_dictionary` —\n  rebuilds `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` from the cache.\n- `npm --prefix tests/e2e run test:local -- tests/issue-221.spec.js` —\n  browser worker regressions pass.\n\n## Upstream-issue reports\n\nNone filed. Same diagnosis as #218 applies: Wiktionary serves correct\ndata, Wikidata serves correct lexemes, the gaps were entirely in our\nseeding pipeline. The polysemy edge cases that surfaced during seeding\n(e.g. `milk` → `доить` because the Wikidata lexeme query returned the\nverb first) are catalogued in `online-research.md` and tracked in the\n\"Future work\" section below — the dictionary captures the right\nsurface for nouns explicitly, side-stepping the issue for the demo.\n\n## Future work\n\n- **Lexeme disambiguation** — the SPARQL query in\n  `src/translation/wikidata.rs` should restrict P5137 joins by\n  lexical category (noun ↔ noun) so `milk` resolves to `молоко`\n  instead of `доить`. Tracked under the polysemy follow-up.\n- **Live Wiktionary fetch in the browser** — the worker can still\n  reach `*.wiktionary.org/w/api.php?...&origin=*` for words not in\n  the dictionary. Now that the dictionary infrastructure exists we\n  can layer a tiny CORS-aware wikitext parser on top.\n- **Sentence-level translation** — the issue asks for \"text of any\n  size\". The current pipeline plus dictionary covers single words and\n  short greetings. A proper sentence pipeline (tokenize → translate\n  per-token → re-inflect via Wiktionary grammar tables) is the\n  long-form follow-up. Tracked in the \"согласованность\" comment in\n  issue #221.\n"

The fetch\n  is same-origin (no CORS), and the JSON ships as a static asset.\n- The browser worker can therefore resolve every common noun in the\n  seed list **without** crossing the network, while keeping the\n  existing registry as a back-up for greeting phrases.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three new tests\n  — `issue_221_common_russian_nouns_translate_to_english`,\n  `issue_221_common_english_nouns_translate_to_russian`, and\n  `issue_221_unquoted_common_noun_works_in_all_languages` — fail\n  loudly when any of помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or\n  their English counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — same prompts as the Rust tests, plus the round-trip\n  `ru→en→ru` to prove the dictionary keeps semantics symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.log` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; The order mirrors the\ninvestigation timeline; each reference was followed against live\nendpoints before any code change.\n\n## Wiktionary API\n\n- **`action=parse&prop=wikitext`** — the pipeline pulls raw wikitext\n  for every page rather than the rendered HTML. The wikitext is the\n  only place where the `{{trans-top}}` / `{{перев-блок}}` sense\n  blocks are stable, since rendered HTML strips template metadata.\n- **CORS** — MediaWiki accepts `&origin=*` for anonymous read-only\n  GETs across all `*.wiktionary.org` editions. This is what\n  `fetchWiktionaryEntry` already uses for the external lookup\n  fallback. We **could** add live translation fetch in the worker on\n  top of this, but the current pull request opts for a pre-compiled\n  dictionary because the demo must work without leaking the\n  user's browsing patterns to Wikimedia. See PR #222 discussion.\n- **Translation subpages** — high-traffic English entries (e.g.\n  `apple`, `book`, `milk`) keep translation tables on a `/translations`\n  subpage referenced by `{{see translation subpage|...}}`. The Rust\n  pipeline already tries this fallback (`pipeline.rs` stage 1a).\n\n## Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join\n\n- **P5137** (`item for this sense`) is the canonical link from a\n  Wiktionary sense to a language-neutral Q-item. Joining two\n  lexemes through P5137 gives us a deterministic\n  `meaning_id (Q…)` regardless of which side served the trigger.\n- **Polysemy gotcha** — when a single surface form has both noun and\n  verb lexemes (e.g. English `milk` → noun `L4514` and verb\n  `L4514-S1`), the SPARQL query returns whichever lexeme appears\n  first. The current code path picks `L4514` and follows its sole\n  P5137 sense to whatever Wikidata calls the canonical Russian form,\n  landing on `доить` (the verb \"to milk\") instead of `молоко`. This\n  is a **known limitation** flagged in the case-study future work;\n  the dictionary work-around captures `molokó` directly for the\n  demo.\n- **502 errors** — the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint occasionally returns\n  HTTP 502 under load. The pipeline records the error in the\n  provenance trace and falls back to the Wiktionary block-level\n  result instead of failing the whole translation.\n\n## Russian Wiktionary specifics\n\n- The `=== Перевод ===` section is the reverse-lookup anchor. The\n  Russian edition is the densest source of `ru → other` data because\n  English Wiktionary's `ru:` columns are often sparse for\n  intermediate-frequency nouns.\n- Inflection templates (`{{сущ-ru|...}}`) carry the full declension\n  paradigm in wikitext. We do **not** parse them in this PR — the\n  alias generator hard-codes the common suffix tables — but\n  parsing them is the right long-term answer for issues like\n  `Переведи \"помидоры\" на английский.` (plural form).\n\n## Browser CORS constraints\n\n- Web workers run in the same origin as the host page (GitHub\n  Pages: `link-assistant.github.io`). They can `fetch()` any\n  same-origin asset (the seed bundles, the WASM blob, and now\n  `translation-dictionary.json`).\n- Cross-origin fetches succeed only when the remote server emits\n  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Wiktionary's `api.php` does so\n  when you pass `&origin=*`. So a live fallback is technically\n  possible — see the \"Future work\" section in the README.\n\n## Related upstream issues\n\n- Wikimedia phabricator T241992 — long-standing request to include\n  P5137 senses in `wbsearchentities`.
